title: Docs article
blurb: The 'Building an accessible dialog' guide went from a stock Docusaurus page with 105-character lines and five admonitions to a 70ch reading page whose dialog example actually runs, tracing focus and logging every close reason as you use it.

persona.name: Leo Marchetti
persona.role: Frontend lead implementing a delete confirmation
persona.goal: Read the dialog guide once, copy the right snippet and understand the focus and closing rules without hunting.

before.verdict: Readable, but it is every Docusaurus site: stock green, stock Prism, and five admonitions where one belongs. Lines run past 100 characters on a laptop, the one real warning about backdrop close sits between filler notes and a 'Danger' that contradicts the props table, and the focus rules can only be read about, not tried.

after.verdict: A docs page built for reading and for trying. The snippet runs right under the code: open it, Tab, press Esc or click outside, and a four-step trace shows where focus went while a log names the close reason. The props table becomes cards on a phone, and the checklist links back to the section that covers each rule.

critique.title: Lines too long to read
critique.detail: The doc column is Docusaurus's `max-width: 75%` of a 1320px container, so body lines run to ~105 characters at 1440px. Readers lose their place at every line break on a Read page.

critique.title: Admonition overload
critique.detail: Note, tip, info, warning and danger all appear in one guide, each with an icon and a 5px coloured border-left. Two are filler ('Focus is trapped automatically'), the danger box contradicts the closeOnEsc row in the props table, and the one real warning about backdrop close gets lost.

critique.title: Could be any Docusaurus site
critique.detail: Default #2e8555 green, the stock navbar, stock Prism github theme and stock footer. Nothing says Grain UI; Leo can't tell this guide from the last five library docs he read.

critique.title: Focus rules you can only imagine
critique.detail: Initial focus, focus return and close reasons are explained in static snippets. The guide is about behaviour, but there is nothing to open, Tab through or press Esc on.

critique.title: Props table crushed on phones
critique.detail: The four-column table is `display: block; overflow: auto`, so at 390px the Description column wraps to one or two words per line and Default sits in a narrow strip.

critique.title: Emoji headings and a fake checklist
critique.detail:
The h1 ends in 🚀, the last h2 in ✅, and the checklist is six ✅ lines joined with
, so screen readers announce 'check mark button' six times and there is no list to navigate. The copy button stays at opacity 0 until hover, so touch users never see it.

changes.before: .doc { flex: 0 0 75%; max-width: 75% } inside a 1320px container (~105ch lines at 1440px)
changes.why: Lines stay at a comfortable 65–72 characters at every viewport width.

changes.before: Docusaurus defaults: h1 3rem, h2 2rem, h3 1.5rem, all weight 700 in the system font stack
changes.after: h1 clamp(2.25rem, 1.7rem + 1.6vw, 3rem) at weight 680, -0.032em; h2 1.625rem; h3 1.25rem; Inter with font-optical-sizing: auto
changes.why: A clear scale makes the guide skimmable, and optical sizing keeps the big title tight and the body open.

changes.before: Stock Prism github theme: pre { background: #f6f8fa; font-size: 90% }, copy button opacity: 0 until hover
changes.after: pre code { font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.7; color: #26242f on #f5f4f9 } (dark: #e4e2ee on #1a1922)
changes.why: Code is the most-copied part of the page, so it gets a readable size, tuned token colours for each theme and a copy button you can see.

changes.before: 5 admonition kinds (note, tip, info, warning, danger), each with an icon and border-left: 5px solid in its own colour
changes.after: Two styles: neutral note on --surface-2, semantic warning only for real risk, icon plus title, no stripe
changes.why: When warnings are rare, the one about backdrop close actually gets read.

changes.before: Docusaurus defaults: sidebar behind a hamburger drawer, TOC as a collapsed 'On this page' box
changes.after: Rails are position: sticky; top: var(--topbar). ≤1240px: TOC becomes <details>. ≤900px: nav becomes a <details> 'Docs menu'
changes.why: The article stays first on every screen size, and navigation and the TOC are one tap away without leaving the page.

changes.before: Icon-only search pill on mobile; props table as display: block; overflow: auto with no label
changes.after: :focus-visible rings, sr-only search label with ⌘K, props table in a labelled scroll region
changes.why: The page works by keyboard, and the props table scrolls on small screens instead of crushing its columns.

changes.before: Static code block; the reader has to imagine what focus does
changes.after: Live example under the snippet: 'Delete atlas-web…' opens a real <dialog>, a 4-node trace (Trigger → Cancel → Delete project → Back to trigger) lights up as focus moves, and a log reads onOpenChange(false) · reason: "escape"
changes.why: The rules the article explains (initial focus, trap, return focus, close reasons) can be checked by hand in five seconds.

changes.after: In the example, a backdrop click is ignored with a 2px nudge and the log 'backdrop click ignored · closeOnBackdrop={false}'; deleting strikes the row and focus lands on 'Undo delete' (returnFocus={listRef})
changes.why: The warning callout and the returnFocus section are shown working, not just described.

changes.before: Props table scrolls sideways on phones
changes.after: ≤600px: each prop becomes a card with labelled Type and Default (data-label); no horizontal scroll at 320px
changes.why: Leo can read the API on his phone without panning a table.

changes.before: Checklist as six ✅ emoji lines joined with
changes.after: Numbered checklist cards that each link to their section, plus a 'Was this guide helpful?' Yes/No with a live thank-you
changes.why: Each rule points to where it's explained, so the list doubles as a review tool.

tells: Default Docusaurus green instead of the product's own brand
No max-width measure on prose (~105ch lines)
Five admonition types on one page
Filler admonitions that restate the prose
